prompt: What is the product when 4-phenyl-3-buten-2-one is hydrogenated over a palladium catalyst at room temperature and atmospheric pressure?

choices.text: 4-Phenyl-2-butanone; only the C=C double bond is reduced
4-Cyclohexyl-2-butanone; the C=C bond and the aromatic ring are both reduced
choices.why: Aromatic rings are inert to hydrogenation under conditions that reduce typical alkene double bonds.

choices.text: 4-Phenyl-2-butanol; the C=C bond and the ketone are both reduced
choices.why: Neither the benzene ring nor the ketone carbonyl group is affected under these conditions.

choices.text: Butylbenzene; the C=C bond and the C=O group are both reduced to CH2 groups
choices.why: Reduction of C=O to CH2 over Pd works for aryl alkyl ketones, but this carbonyl isn't next to the ring, and the section says it is not affected.

explanation: Aromatic rings are inert to catalytic hydrogenation under conditions that reduce typical alkene double bonds, so an alkene can be reduced selectively in the presence of an aromatic ring. 4-Phenyl-3-buten-2-one is reduced to 4-phenyl-2-butanone over palladium at room temperature and atmospheric pressure; neither the ring nor the ketone is affected.

prompt: When 4-phenyl-3-buten-2-one is hydrogenated over Pd at room temperature and 1 atm, how many moles of H2 are taken up per mole of starting material?
explanation: Only the C=C double bond is reduced, so one mole of H2 is used, giving 4-phenyl-2-butanone. The aromatic ring and the ketone carbonyl group are untouched under these conditions.

prompt: Which conditions will hydrogenate an aromatic ring to a cyclohexane?

choices.text: H2 with Pt at several hundred atmospheres, or with rhodium on carbon
H2 over palladium at room temperature and atmospheric pressure
choices.why: Those conditions reduce alkene double bonds but leave aromatic rings untouched.

choices.text: Aqueous KMnO4, which cleaves alkene double bonds
choices.why: KMnO4 is an oxidizing agent; it oxidizes alkyl side chains and leaves the ring alone.

choices.text: Iron and acid, followed by base, as used for nitro groups
choices.why: Fe and acid reduce a nitro group to an amino group; they don't reduce the ring.

explanation: To hydrogenate an aromatic ring, it's necessary either to use a platinum catalyst with hydrogen gas at a pressure of several hundred atmospheres or to use a more effective catalyst such as rhodium on carbon. Under these conditions, aromatic rings are converted into cyclohexanes.

prompt: o-Xylene is hydrogenated over rhodium on carbon to give 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane. How many moles of H2 are taken up per mole of o-xylene?
explanation: o-Xylene is C8H10 and 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane is C8H16, so 3 mol of H2 add to the ring (one for each of the three double bonds in the Kekulé structure). Forcing conditions, such as Rh/C or Pt at high pressure, are needed.

prompt: What is the product when 4-tert-butylphenol is hydrogenated under conditions that reduce aromatic rings?

choices.text: 4-tert-Butylcyclohexanol
4-tert-Butylcyclohexanone
choices.why: The ring is converted into a cyclohexane, and the –OH group stays as an alcohol.

choices.text: tert-Butylbenzene, by loss of the OH group
choices.why: The ring itself is reduced; the hydroxyl group is kept.

choices.text: No reaction, because phenols can't be hydrogenated
choices.why: With a platinum catalyst at high pressure, or with rhodium on carbon, the aromatic ring is reduced to a cyclohexane.

explanation: Under forcing conditions (Pt at several hundred atmospheres, or rhodium on carbon), aromatic rings are converted into cyclohexanes. o-Xylene gives 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, and 4-tert-butylphenol gives 4-tert-butylcyclohexanol.

prompt: What is formed when propiophenone (C6H5COCH2CH3) is catalytically hydrogenated over a palladium catalyst?

choices.text: Propylbenzene
1-Phenyl-1-propanol
choices.why: Over Pd, an aryl alkyl ketone's carbonyl group is converted all the way into a CH2 group.

choices.text: Propylcyclohexane
choices.why: The ring isn't reduced over Pd; only the benzylic carbonyl group is converted to CH2.

choices.text: No reaction, because ketones aren't reduced by catalytic hydrogenation
choices.why: Dialkyl ketones aren't reduced under these conditions, but aryl alkyl ketones are activated by the ring and reduced to alkylbenzenes.

explanation: In the same way that an aromatic ring activates a neighboring benzylic C–H toward oxidation, it also activates a benzylic carbonyl group toward reduction. An aryl alkyl ketone such as propiophenone is converted into an alkylbenzene, propylbenzene, by catalytic hydrogenation over palladium.

prompt: Why is propylbenzene made by Friedel–Crafts acylation with propanoyl chloride followed by hydrogenation, rather than by direct alkylation with 1-chloropropane?

choices.text: Alkylation with a primary halide gives rearranged products; acyl cations don't rearrange
Direct alkylation fails because 1-chloropropane is a vinylic halide
choices.why: 1-Chloropropane is an ordinary primary alkyl halide. The problem is rearrangement of its carbocation.

choices.text: Acylation is faster because acyl chlorides are more electrophilic than aromatic rings
choices.why: The advantage is that acyl cations don't rearrange, so the straight propyl chain is kept.

choices.text: Direct alkylation gives only a ketone, which must then be reduced
choices.why: Alkylation gives alkylbenzenes, not ketones. The trouble is the mixture caused by carbocation rearrangement.

explanation: Friedel–Crafts acylation followed by reduction gives a primary alkylbenzene, so this two-step sequence circumvents the carbocation rearrangement problems of direct alkylation with a primary alkyl halide (Section 16.3). Benzene with 1-chloropropane and AlCl3 gives a mixture of two products.

prompt: Which ketone would NOT have its C=O group converted into CH2 by catalytic hydrogenation over palladium?

choices.text: 3-Pentanone, CH3CH2COCH2CH3
Acetophenone, C6H5COCH3
choices.why: Acetophenone is an aryl alkyl ketone, so its benzylic carbonyl group is reduced, giving ethylbenzene.

choices.text: Propiophenone, C6H5COCH2CH3
choices.why: Propiophenone is the section's example: it is reduced to propylbenzene.

choices.text: C6H5COCH(CH3)2
choices.why: This is an aryl alkyl ketone, so its carbonyl group is next to the ring and is reduced to CH2.

explanation: The conversion of a carbonyl group into a methylene group (C=O → CH2) by catalytic hydrogenation is limited to aryl alkyl ketones; dialkyl ketones such as 3-pentanone are not reduced under these conditions. A more general method appears in Section 19.9.

prompt: What is formed when m-nitroacetophenone is hydrogenated over palladium on carbon?

choices.text: m-Ethylaniline; both the ketone and the nitro group are reduced
m-Ethylnitrobenzene; only the ketone is reduced
choices.why: A nitro group is reduced to an amino group under these conditions, so the nitro group doesn't survive.

choices.text: m-Aminoacetophenone; only the nitro group is reduced
choices.why: The aryl alkyl ketone is also reduced, to an ethyl group.

choices.text: 1-Ethyl-3-nitrocyclohexane; the ring is reduced too
choices.why: Pd at ordinary conditions doesn't reduce the aromatic ring.

explanation: Catalytic reduction of aryl alkyl ketones is not compatible with a nitro substituent on the ring, because a nitro group is reduced to an amino group under the reaction conditions. m-Nitroacetophenone gives m-ethylaniline.

prompt: How would you prepare diphenylmethane, (C6H5)2CH2, from benzene and an acid chloride?

choices.text: 1. C6H5COCl, AlCl3; 2. H2/Pd
1. C6H5COCl, AlCl3; 2. KMnO4
choices.why: KMnO4 is an oxidizing agent. Turning the C=O into CH2 needs reduction, by H2 over Pd.

choices.text: 1. CH3COCl, AlCl3; 2. H2/Pd
choices.why: This sequence makes ethylbenzene. A second phenyl group requires benzoyl chloride, C6H5COCl.

choices.text: 1. Chlorobenzene, AlCl3
choices.why: Aryl halides don't react in Friedel–Crafts reactions, because aryl carbocations are too high in energy.

explanation: Exercise 16.9.1: Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene with benzoyl chloride, C6H5COCl, and AlCl3 gives the aryl ketone C6H5COC6H5. Catalytic hydrogenation over Pd then converts the benzylic C=O group into CH2, giving diphenylmethane.
